_doc: Hand-maintained layer of the robot BOM (owner 2026-11-20: generated, but agents must be able to maintain and adjust it). robot/body/bom/build.py reads this file together with the selected body manifest and writes the BOM; every value here wins over the generated default and is marked `source: lines.json`. Edit it like any data file and commit. Sections: `lines` group manifest parts into one buy / make line (first match wins; `match` = part-name globs, `roles` = manifest roles, `motor` = the parts' manifest `motor` field) and carry what the CAD cannot know (supplier, part number, price, notes, make_buy: make | buy | included | context). Parts no line matches get a generated line: printed parts one line per part, standard hardware one line per spec (robot/body/bom/hardware.py), everything else one line per name stem (side prefix and trailing index removed). `manual_lines` are items with no CAD (filament, glue, wire). `part_overrides` move one part to another line, exclude it with a reason, or add notes. `quantity` on a line overrides the count from the CAD (the BOM shows both).

lines.name: M2 plain spacer (clearance bore 2.2) 5.8 across corners x 5.0 mm, hex, no thread

spec.standard: plain hex spacer, clearance bore (no thread)

lines.notes: Camera board to carrier plate (8: 4 per camera). Owner 2026-11-22 (T-5bqc3m): the ISO 4762 M2 screw is driven from the camera front through washer, board and this spacer into an internally threaded steel sleeve in the carrier, so the spacer needs no thread. The CAD still carries the supplier's M2 F-F standoff mesh (bore 1.6) under the old part names as the stand-in; the bought part is a plain spacer of the same outside and length. Supplier and part number not found yet.

lines.name: Threaded steel sleeve M2, 3.5 OD x 2.0 mm (press-fit), head carrier camera posts (8) and mic post 1
lines.notes: Internally threaded 304 steel sleeve pressed into the head carrier (owner 2026-11-22, T-5bqc3m): 8 camera posts (plate front face to 0.5 mm behind the plate; the ISO 4762 M2x10 is driven from the camera front through washer, board and plain spacer, engagement 2.0 mm = 1 d) and the lower mic post in the wing (M2x4 from the mic board, engagement 2.0 mm). Same pattern as the stage-1 threaded sleeves of the torso (T-bv7bwe). ASSUMPTION: thread modelled at the ISO 724 minor diameter 1.567 mm; no supplier of a press-in M2 threaded sleeve of OD 3.5 mm (wall about 1 mm) found, it may have to be made. Generated by robot/body/neck-head/neck_parts.py; counted from the sleeve STEP, which also carries the neck-root and compute sleeves.

manual_lines.name: Threaded steel sleeve M2, 3.5 OD x 1.17 mm (press-fit), head carrier upper mic post
manual_lines.notes: In the CAD (combined__head_sensor_compute_carrier_steel_sleeves, 10th threaded sleeve) but below the BOM sleeve counter's 1.5 mm minimum length, so the generated line does not count it. Length = the thread of the M2x3 screw that fits under the head skin (tip 0.3 mm clear); the wing there is only 0.83 mm thick (skin taper), the sleeve stands 0.34 mm proud on a 0.7 mm rim. Same sleeve assumption as hw:threaded sleeves of the camera posts.
